img.caption: Figure 1: Training-free framework for single-turn set-valued intent understanding with calibrated refusal. Given a context-sparse query q, we retrieve Top-K candidates from a zero-annotation external intent knowledge base (KB) that stores intent prototypes and example utterance vectors, while a black-box LLM reasons over the retrieved evidence and returns a primary intent, an ordered set of secondary intents, and a self-reported confidence. The two signals are converted to ranks and fused by s(q) = g(stats_ret, Conf_LLM) with alpha = 0.1. A split conformal calibration on a held-out set derives a threshold tau_cal that guarantees finite-sample coverage P(Y in S_hat(q)) >= 1-alpha = 0.90 under exchangeability, optimizing a set-level Jaccard risk rather than pointwise label coverage. The fused score s(q) is then routed through an adaptive three-state decision whose thresholds tau_lo, tau_hi are calibrated at FPR95: confident queries release a 1-intent set for downstream routing, ambiguous queries return a minimal set of 2-3 candidates for user clarification, and out-of-scope queries are rejected with an empty set for human escalation. The entire inference path requires no gradient updates and no classifier head; light fine-tuning (LoRA/SetFit) is shown only as an optional accuracy comparison. Main results use top-1 retrieval (K_r=1); the K=10 candidate pool is shown for illustration.
